first_heading: ## Appendix A — The Complete Identifier Registry by Prefix

may_not: remove or weaken the Severity 1 floor
remove the qualification gate itself (posture only)
roles_rules.surface: Delivery Operations Hub, tenant admin area
scope_conditions: Current-value changes only; bound changes are floor-register changes and therefore critical class
Registry validates against the bound and rejects an out-of-bound value outright

may: write retention horizon, usage-ladder thresholds, tier assignment, suspension state, pilot status, Regulated-Industry mode toggle, feature enablement, legal holds, JBS access grants
may_not: initiate compliance suspension outside the platform-initiated path

may: approve changes to the platform floor register (critical class)
may_not: turn off any of the six enforced invariants
scope_conditions: The evaluation gate binds every console operator including the root
The six enforced invariants render locked in Super Admin settings with no off position for any account including the root

may: release a lot, unit or run held under the Severity 1 floor
scope_conditions: Severity 1 floor is an immovable minimum: automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release
Tenants may add actions above the floor, never remove or weaken it

business_rules.statement: An identifier that does not match a prefix in the Appendix A registry table is a defect.
Identifiers are never reader-facing titles: narrative writes the human sentence and the identifier sits beside it in metadata, tables and traceability appendices.
A tenant can always be stricter than the platform default. They can never be looser. The platform refuses the value and tells them the limit, rather than accepting it and quietly writing a note.
The register rejects, it does not log: a looser-than-floor value fails at the point of entry with the bound stated.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Platform floor register at point of entry

business_rules.statement: Changes to the floor register itself are critical class, meaning the root account approves them.
Specification gates are hard, platform-fixed, on and immovable: no tenant off-switch; a failed specification capture blocks progression.
Evaluation gate is hard and platform-fixed: no capability enables with pending or failing scenarios; it binds every console operator including the root.
Severity 1 floor: automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release. Tenants may add actions above the floor, never remove or weaken it.
Minimum genealogy depth is one level plus full rework history; tenants may not reduce it.
Qualification-expiry warnings: earlier only, never later. Default 14, 7, 1 and 0 days.
Evidence immutability, cross-tenant isolation, on-device severity classification and audit completeness are platform-fixed by construction rather than by register entry.

The six enforced invariants render locked in Super Admin settings with no off position for any account including the root: evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, and the one-transaction audit guarantee.
One console object exists per tenant holding every setting as three values (platform default, bound, current value); it is the single enforcement point of the configurability principle.
business_rules.applies_to: All tenant settings, all write paths

business_rules.statement: The tag pre-populates but never decides: tag to qualification-set mapping is pre-population only.
Legal holds are dual-approved on release; a hold suspends tiering and compliance-driven deletion.
Data is never purged, it tiers; the 15-year horizon is a default hot-retrievability horizon per tenant.
Deletion occurs only where a named standard requires it; without the client-supplied list, the no-purge model has an unbounded exception.
Nothing ITAR-flavoured is committed to any prospect before the certifications answer.
The command channel is defined once in Part I and cross-referenced thereafter.
Notifications are constrained to in-app and email channels at V1; commands are constrained to the five command-channel classes.
Where Appendix F and Chapter 51 disagree, Chapter 51 wins; Appendix F is a pointer only.
If any chapter states a different number for the same thing than the Numbers Canon, the canon table wins and the chapter is wrong.
Where a value's normative definition lives in a Part rather than in §1.7, the owning section is authoritative and is the one cited.

The blueprint uses full names in narrative; a short form appears only in parentheses immediately after the full name on first use in a chapter, and never as a reader-facing title. AVIIXA and JBS keep their brand forms.
Where a chapter uses one of the canonical complex terms without defining it at first use, gate 29 fails.
The assembler recounts every Appendix L count against the finished document before it is issued; where the recount disagrees with the table, the recount wins.
A count that is not reconciled must not be quoted in a commercial document.
No row in the final-counts table is left Open, because an estimated count in a final-counts table reads as a fact.

Neither Recommendation — R&D (derived) nor (sourced) is a SoW Fact, neither is a client requirement, and no Appendix M finding may be presented to the client as something the Statement of Work obliges. That prohibition is absolute.
Research can validate a position, challenge it, or open a question. It can never become an obligation on the client, and can never be quietly folded into a chapter as though the source had said it.
A web source without an access date is not a citation; every source cited was fetched and read on 2026-08-15 and the date is repeated on every citation.
Absence from public documentation is reported as absence from documentation and never as absence from a product.
Vendor marketing claims are attributed to the vendor making them and treated as evidence of what that vendor's product claims, never as evidence of what the industry does.

No DEC-RND- decision may be presented to the client as a requirement, as a defect, or as something the Statement of Work obliges. A rejected DEC-RND- decision is closed by the rejection and needs no further justification.
A source contradiction cannot be rejected; it can only be answered. A research recommendation can be declined, and the blueprint stays correct.
A row says Ahead only where no comparable published source documents the capability; the correct reading is 'not documented by comparable vendors', never 'nobody does this'.
No M.10 row is a commitment, a roadmap or a requirement, and no row should be quoted in a commercial document without the finding behind it.
Every finding whose own text says a client decision is needed carries exactly one DEC-RND- identifier.
Every DEC-RND- identifier appears in the complete decision index at section 51.12.
In sections M.1 to M.8, no line carrying a DEC-RND- identifier also asserts that the recommendation is required, must be implemented, or is a SoW Fact.
Every finding in sections M.1 to M.8 carries at least one source link and the access date, resolving any back-reference to a source introduced by an earlier finding.
Every source link used in the findings appears in the register at section M.9.
No chapter may claim complete coverage while an open decision remains in its scope.
An open decision is listed with its owner, so the reader knows whose answer unblocks it.
A decision answered after publication does not silently upgrade the coverage claim: the dashboard is re-run and republished.
No fabricated contractual value appears anywhere in Chapters 54 and 55.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-HON-005 fabricated-value scan; pass condition zero findings

business_rules.statement: Every value the source does not state is marked open rather than invented: no SLA, RTO, RPO, retry limit, timeout, queue limit, offline duration, retention period, confidence threshold, model expiry, approval window or account limit has been fabricated.
Every failure narrative terminates in a named terminal safe state, and no narrative promises uninterrupted operation where continuation would be unsafe.
The terminal safe state of the honesty statement is that the blueprint remains in the conditional state and says so on its face; there is no state in which coverage is asserted without evidence.

decisions.question: Which scheduled jobs are time-critical for compliance and which are merely periodic (flexible time windows)
decisions.impact: Any job with a compliance-visible timestamp cannot use dispersal

decisions.question: Is scheduling fairness part of the tenant-isolation promise, or is isolation a data-access guarantee only
decisions.impact: 'Ran 40 minutes late' and 'did not run' have different regulatory weight; the blueprint currently reads as data-access only

decisions.question: Google's distributed cron: prefer skipping to double-launching, and name jobs by scheduled time
decisions.adopted_working_position: No decision needed on the naming convention (implementation detail); skip-versus-duplicate is captured in DEC-RND-SCHED-001
decisions.impact: Name work by its scheduled instant for free idempotency; write intent before acting

decisions.question: Whether to adopt a durable-execution engine (Temporal) for the agent orchestrator
decisions.impact: Foundational platform choice with hiring and operational consequences; every LLM call must be an Activity

decisions.question: Managed versus self-hosted Temporal
decisions.impact: Self-hosting adds a database tier and a shard-count decision that cannot be walked back; managed raises data-residency and tenant-isolation questions

decisions.question: Whether the never-purge rule applies to operational plumbing (outbox rows, lease records, scheduler bookkeeping) or only to evidence
decisions.impact: Left ambiguous, this becomes a storage-growth argument in year three

decisions.question: Is 'two workers never touch the same record' an assumption the process guarantees, or a hope the software should enforce (fencing tokens)
decisions.status: open, research-surfaced (declinable); described as the highest-stakes in this area
decisions.impact: Changes the offline-first sync contract; devices must carry and return the version they read

decisions.question: What is the maximum supported offline duration for a device (sizing the idempotency window)
decisions.impact: One number sizes the idempotency window, the sync conflict horizon and the on-device queue; Stripe's 24-hour retention is far too short

decisions.question: For each scheduled job family, the intended post-outage behaviour (overlap policy, catchup window, pause-on-failure, jitter)
decisions.impact: Two credible systems chose opposite defaults (Kubernetes stops past 100 misses; Temporal's catchup window defaults to one year)

decisions.question: A small fixed role set is normal practice; custom roles are a permanent maintenance liability
decisions.adopted_working_position: No decision for v1; the named trigger is the first customer needing one permission where every role carrying it also carries something they refuse to grant
decisions.impact: Access-control chapter and the role-and-scope model

decisions.question: Is creator-cannot-approve enforced optimistically on-device and re-verified at sync (with possible reversal), or is approval blocked offline when provenance cannot be proved
decisions.impact: Materially different products for a frontline worker; the rule is object/history-based, not role-based SSD or DSD

decisions.question: Are the three orthogonal scopes simultaneously active or singly selected per session
decisions.impact: Cheap to decide now and expensive to change after the mobile app ships

decisions.question: Do we stamp evidence with the authorisation epoch, and what is the defined response when evidence arrives signed under a superseded authorisation
decisions.status: open, research-surfaced (declinable); described as the single highest-value addition this research suggests
decisions.impact: Offline authorisation, sync-conflict model and evidence immutability; detection without a defined response is worse than useless

decisions.question: Whether access-authorisation changes are treated as evidence-class immutable records with the same retention as operational evidence
decisions.impact: Annex 11 §12.3 gap: evidence is immutable but the authority under which evidence was created is not

decisions.question: Approval-before-access or notify-and-terminate; the auto-approval carve-out and how it is logged; the published exclusion list
decisions.impact: Super Admin platform console; AVIIXA is ahead on termination, behind on consent

decisions.question: The field set and retention for the support-access log, and whether accessor identity is disclosed at individual or role level
decisions.impact: Super Admin console and the Delivery Operations Hub's audit surface; publishing accessor location and employer is a personal-data disclosure about AVIIXA staff

decisions.question: Whether AVIIXA wants to claim comprehensive support-access accountability via session recording
decisions.adopted_working_position: No for v1 if the exclusion list is published
decisions.impact: Super Admin console; a recorded session containing tenant PII is sensitive data stored twice

decisions.question: The activation duration and approval requirement per Super Admin capability tier, and the number, custody and dual-control arrangement for break-glass accounts
decisions.impact: Bounds damage from a compromised AVIIXA staff credential; bootstrap hazard if the approval path depends on AVIIXA's own systems

decisions.question: Whether AVIIXA offers a dedicated-database (silo) tier at all
decisions.adopted_working_position: No decision on the isolation principle itself
decisions.impact: Multi-tenancy chapter; 'compliance pushback' is a named expected outcome of a pooled model

decisions.question: What assurance level the Frontline Worker Application claims, and whether the trust window is clock-bound only or clock-and-shift-bound

decisions.question: The minimum touch target size and spacing, decided once and written into the design system
options: primary targets at least 18 mm with at least 5 mm clear spacing
decisions.impact: Constrains every screen and every authored step template; 18 mm targets mean 4-6 primary actions on a 5-inch handheld

decisions.question: The deployment baseline: which devices, which glove type, screen protector or not (touch panel mode)
decisions.status: open, research-surfaced (declinable); a deployment-baseline decision, not a software decision
decisions.impact: Glove support is a fleet configuration property, and the vendor default (Finger Only) is the wrong one

decisions.question: WCAG 2.2 AA on all five surfaces, or AA on worker-facing surfaces and A elsewhere
options: AA on worker-facing surfaces and A elsewhere
decisions.adopted_working_position: WCAG 2.2 Level AA, evaluated per EN 301 549 clause 11 for the native application, satisfies both EU and DOJ instruments
decisions.impact: The realistic driver is procurement, not enforcement; none of the instruments automatically binds AVIIXA

decisions.question: Whether authored-content accessibility checks block publication or only warn
decisions.impact: Standards and Operations Studio; imported legacy content must be grandfathered explicitly or migration blocks on day one

decisions.question: Whether the Severity 1 screen is modal and blocking on the device until acknowledged
decisions.adopted_working_position: No decision needed for adding haptic feedback
decisions.impact: Changes what a worker can do in the seconds after a freeze; colour must not carry the freeze state alone

decisions.question: Whether a step may be published with only one locale complete, and if so whether Spanish-only workers are blocked from that step or shown English with a warning
options: block publication until both locales exist
decisions.status: open, research-surfaced (declinable); a safety decision disguised as a workflow decision
decisions.impact: Authored-per-locale means every instruction change is two authoring and two review tasks

decisions.question: Whether the client will staff a terminology owner for a controlled-language house style and glossary
decisions.adopted_working_position: No to adopting ASD-STE100 wholesale (do not); a 20-rule house style plus a term glossary is the realistic move
decisions.impact: Standards and Operations Studio; the rule set is worthless unattended and decays within a year

decisions.question: Whether EU deployment is in scope within the planning horizon (which forces an N-language locale mechanism)
options: in scope - locale mechanism N-language from day one
decisions.impact: EU Machinery Regulation sets the instruction language by Member State; 10 years online minimum versus AVIIXA's 15-year horizon

decisions.question: Does 'no pace or timer' bind only the worker's screen, or the supervisor's screens too
decisions.status: open, research-surfaced (declinable); described as the significant one
decisions.impact: Answering 'worker only' makes the position mostly cosmetic; binding supervisors removes a feature clients will ask for

decisions.question: Whether workers get a transparency screen and a challenge action against agent interpretations
decisions.impact: Product-scope decision with an operational cost tail; interacts with each client's labour-relations context

decisions.question: Who controls the work-instruction difficulty level (worker, supervisor, or qualification record), and whether the level in force is part of the immutable evidence for a step
decisions.impact: Expertise reversal: a level set once and never revisited is actively worse than no guidance

decisions.question: Shared or assigned devices per tenant, and which identity provider
decisions.impact: Changes the sign-in design and the offline credential-caching requirement materially
